executiveSummary: Apex presents high operational and data protection risk. The recovery plan has never been tested, a 24-hour recovery point permits significant data loss, and international processing lacks documented transfer safeguards. Validate resilience and transfer arrangements before placing customer data in the service; obtain an updated penetration test.

findings.finding: Disaster recovery plan has never been tested
findings.description: Apex's continuity summary states that its disaster recovery plan has never been tested and that recovery steps remain in draft. There is no completed exercise to validate those procedures for its laboratory information service.
findings.whyItMatters: During a major outage, Apex may discover that the draft steps cannot restore the LIMS reliably, delaying access to laboratory records and workflows. An exercise is needed to demonstrate that staff, backups and dependencies can support recovery before production reliance.

evidence.quote: The disaster recovery plan has never been tested. Recovery steps remain a draft.

findings.recommendedFollowUp: Please schedule and complete a disaster recovery exercise and share measured recovery results before production onboarding.

findings.finding: 24-hour recovery point risks a full day of data loss
findings.description: Apex specifies a 24-hour recovery point objective and says daily snapshots are its only recovery mechanism. This permits a recovery point up to a day behind the latest laboratory records, exceeding the review's four-hour target.
findings.whyItMatters: After a failure, customers could need to reconstruct up to a day's laboratory entries and reconcile work completed since the last snapshot. Decide whether that potential loss fits the intended LIMS use and ask Apex to demonstrate more frequent recovery points if it does not.

evidence.quote: The recovery point objective is 24 hours. Daily snapshots are the only recovery mechanism.

findings.recommendedFollowUp: Can you support a four-hour RPO and supply evidence of backup restoration and transaction recovery?

findings.description: Apex's data protection policy says no signed Standard Contractual Clauses or UK transfer addendum are currently in place. The submitted pack therefore does not establish documented safeguards for its international processing arrangement.
findings.whyItMatters: The customer cannot confirm from Apex's pack which transfer mechanism and assessment support the intended personal-data use. Ask the appropriate privacy reviewer to confirm the applicable safeguards and required documentation before approving that processing arrangement.

evidence.quote: No signed Standard Contractual Clauses or UK transfer addendum are currently in place.

findings.recommendedFollowUp: Please provide executed transfer safeguards, a transfer assessment and the complete processing location register.

findings.description: Apex's questionnaire dates its last independent penetration test to 18 months ago and says no new test has been scheduled. The review has no more recent assurance of the laboratory platform's security testing.
findings.whyItMatters: Changes to Apex's LIMS and its integrations since the last test may not have been independently assessed. Request the test scope, outstanding remediation and a new test date to judge current exposure instead of treating the old report as current assurance.

evidence.quote: The last independent penetration test was completed 18 months ago. A new test has not been scheduled.

findings.recommendedFollowUp: When will the next independent penetration test be completed? Please share the last report and open remediation items.

findings.finding: Overseas storage requires a transfer review
findings.description: Apex's policy places customer data and backups in Singapore and the United States. The disclosed storage footprint needs to be checked against the customer's intended UK/EU data residency and backup requirements.
findings.whyItMatters: If the customer's agreed residency scope excludes those locations, Apex's current hosting arrangement may not fit the proposed contract. Confirm approved primary and backup locations and any UK/EU hosting option; this contractual fit issue is separate from the missing transfer safeguards.

evidence.quote: Customer data and backups are stored in Singapore and the United States.

findings.recommendedFollowUp: Can you offer UK/EU hosting, and document contractual data residency commitments and backup locations?
